Fact.Name: Filer elects to split the direct-deposit refund across two or three accounts (Form 8888)
Fact.Description: User response: the filer wants the refund on Form 1040 line 35a deposited into more than one account, which is what attaching Form 8888 means. A FILER CHOICE, not an arithmetic: "Use Form 8888 if you want us to directly deposit your refund (or part of it) to either two or three accounts at a bank or other financial institution". Asked only after the filer has chosen direct deposit (paymentMethod:/refundViaAch) and entered the first account (paymentMethod:/bankAccount); the split's first row IS that account. Unanswered means no split: every consumer below resolves Complete at its no-election default, and the Form 1040 lines 35a-35d posture is byte-identical to the return before this module existed.

Fact.Name: Form 8888 line 1a, amount to be deposited in the first account
Fact.Description: Form 8888 line 1a, "Amount to be deposited in first account". The FIRST account is paymentMethod:/bankAccount, the account already entered for Form 1040 lines 35b-35d (see /form8888FirstAccount); this is the portion of the refund that goes to it. Floored at zero by the writable; the form's own floor is $1 per deposit ("Each deposit must be at least $1"), which /form8888AnyDepositBelowMinimum enforces as a refusal rather than a silent clamp.

Fact.Name: Form 8888 lines 2 and 3, the additional accounts the refund is split into
Fact.Description: The accounts on Form 8888 lines 2 and 3, in order: the second and (if any) third account the refund is split into. One item is a two-account split, two items a three-account split; the form has no fourth row and is not for a single account, so /form8888AllocationRowCountOutsideForm refuses zero items and three or more. The first account is NOT in this collection: it is paymentMethod:/bankAccount, already held (see the module header). An empty or absent collection on a return that does not elect the split is the no-election return and every consumer resolves Complete at its default on it.

Fact.Name: Form 8888 lines 2b-2d or 3b-3d, an additional account's routing number, type and account number
Fact.Description: The routing number (line b), Checking or Savings (line c) and account number (line d) of an additional account on Form 8888 line 2 or 3. The same validated BankAccount type paymentMethod:/bankAccount uses, so the routing-number and account-number rules ride on the type and are not re-stated here. The form's own guidance for these lines: routing number nine digits, first two digits 01-12 or 21-32; account number up to 17 characters; check exactly one type box.

Fact.Name: Form 8888 line 2a or 3a, amount to be deposited in this additional account
Fact.Description: Form 8888 line 2a ("Amount to be deposited in second account") or line 3a ("Amount to be deposited in third account") for this item. Floored at zero by the writable; the form's $1-per-deposit floor is enforced by refusal (/form8888AnyDepositBelowMinimum).

Fact.Name: Form 8888 additional deposit amount floored at zero
Fact.Description: Non-negative reader for an additional-account deposit amount.

Fact.Name: Form 8888 first deposit amount floored at zero
Fact.Description: Non-negative reader for the first-account deposit amount.

Fact.Name: This Form 8888 row is missing its account or its amount
Fact.Description: True when this additional-account row has been opened but its account (lines b-d) or its amount (line a) is unanswered. A half-answered row is exactly what the form says will delay or reject the deposit ("You haven't given a valid account number or routing transit number"), so it fails CLOSED through the allocation knockout rather than being summed as $0.

Fact.Name: This Form 8888 row's deposit is under the form's $1 floor
Fact.Description: True when this row's amount is answered and below $1: "Each deposit must be at least $1." False when unanswered (that is /rowIncomplete's job).

Fact.Name: Form 8888 line 2c or 3c, the Checking box for this additional account
Fact.Description: The Checking box on Form 8888 line 2c or 3c for this row: TRUE when the account this row carries (../writableAccount) is a checking account. A PROJECTION, NOT NEW INTAKE — the account type already ships on the BankAccount the filer entered once; a printed checkbox needs a Boolean that NAMES the box, and that Boolean is what was missing. The printed line is exclusive, so this fact and /accountIsSavings are the two sides of one answer and are never both true. INCOMPLETE while this row's account is unanswered, which is deliberate: such a row is already refused by /form8888AllocationIncomplete, and a half-answered row must print nothing rather than print an unchecked box the filer never chose. Discharges the line 2c and line 3c DECLARED GAPs named in dictionary/pdf/2025/IRS8888/en/configuration.yml, which asked for exactly this path. Vendored source https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/f8888.pdf.

Fact.Name: Form 8888 line 2c or 3c, the Savings box for this additional account
Fact.Description: The Savings box on Form 8888 line 2c or 3c for this row: TRUE when the account this row carries (../writableAccount) is a savings account. The twin of /accountIsChecking and the same projection of one already-entered account type; the printed line takes one box, not two. INCOMPLETE while this row's account is unanswered, for the reason given on the twin. Discharges the line 2c and line 3c DECLARED GAPs named in dictionary/pdf/2025/IRS8888/en/configuration.yml. Vendored source https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/f8888.pdf.

Fact.Name: The Form 8888 split is in effect: elected, a refund is due, and direct deposit was chosen
Fact.Description:
The election as it reaches the return: /writableSplitRefundAcrossAccounts answered Yes AND a refund is actually due (taxCalculations:/dueRefund, Form 1040 line 35a above zero) AND the filer chose direct deposit (paymentMethod:/refundViaAch). This is what taxCalculations:/form8888Attached reads, and it is COMPLETE-SAFE FALSE: an unanswered election is no election.
THE TWO MOOT CASES ARE MOOT, NOT REFUSED, and that is a deliberate mirror of the return's existing posture. A Yes with no refund due has nothing to split, exactly as an entered /bankAccount with no refund due sends nothing to lines 35b-35d. A Yes with a mailed check chosen is the same shape as paymentMethod:/xmlRefundBankAccount, which resolves to nothing when /refundViaAch is false whatever /bankAccount holds: the earlier answer governs and the later one is unreachable on the printed form (the December 2025 Form 8888 has no paper-check line). The application asks the split only after direct deposit is chosen (INTAKE-GROUPS, group "Form 8888 refund split"), so neither state is a screen a filer can reach in order.

Fact.Name: Form 8888 lines 1b-1d, the first account: the return's own direct-deposit account
Fact.Description: The routing number, type and account number printed on Form 8888 lines 1b-1d, which are paymentMethod:/bankAccount whenever the split is in effect and nothing otherwise. One quantity, one fact: the filer entered this account once for Form 1040 lines 35b-35d, and when Form 8888 is attached those 1040 lines go blank (paymentMethod:/xmlRefundBankAccount) and the account appears here instead. Nothing reads this yet: it is the successor IRS8888 export's and print template's first-row source.

Fact.Name: Form 8888 line 1c, the Checking box for the first account
Fact.Description: The Checking box on Form 8888 line 1c: TRUE when the first account (/form8888FirstAccount, which IS paymentMethod:/bankAccount whenever the split is in effect) is a checking account. A PROJECTION, NOT NEW INTAKE — the account type already ships; the printed checkbox needed a Boolean naming the box. INCOMPLETE on every return that does not elect the split, because /form8888FirstAccount itself resolves to nothing there and this form is not printed at all (dictionary/pdf/2025/IRS8888/en/configuration.yml gates the whole register on includeWhen: /form8888Attached). DO NOT SUBSTITUTE paymentMethod:/refundAccountIsChecking: it reads /xmlRefundBankAccount, which resolves to NOTHING once /form8888Attached is true, so on exactly the population that files this form it is Incomplete and prints nothing -- that trap is recorded in the register itself. Discharges the line 1c DECLARED GAP named in that register, which asked for exactly this path. Vendored source https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/f8888.pdf.

Fact.Name: Form 8888 line 1c, the Savings box for the first account
Fact.Description: The Savings box on Form 8888 line 1c: TRUE when the first account (/form8888FirstAccount) is a savings account. The twin of /form8888FirstAccountIsChecking, the same projection of one already-entered account type, Incomplete on the same no-election population and carrying the same do-not-substitute trap against paymentMethod:/refundAccountIsSavings. Discharges the line 1c DECLARED GAP named in dictionary/pdf/2025/IRS8888/en/configuration.yml. Vendored source https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/f8888.pdf.

Fact.Name: Number of additional accounts entered on Form 8888 lines 2 and 3
Fact.Description: The number of /form8888AdditionalAccounts items; 0 when the collection was never created. The form holds at most two (lines 2 and 3) and a split needs at least one.

Fact.Name: Form 8888 line 5, total allocation of refund: lines 1a + 2a + 3a
Fact.Description: Form 8888 line 5, "Add lines 1a, 2a, and 3a. The total must equal the refund amount shown on your tax return." Line 1a is /writableFirstAccountDepositAmount; lines 2a and 3a are the amounts on /form8888AdditionalAccounts. $0 when the split is not in effect or the collection was never created (complete-safe for the no-election return). When the split IS in effect this fact is deliberately NOT complete-safe: an unanswered line 1a or row amount leaves it Incomplete, and /form8888AllocationIncomplete refuses the return rather than summing a $0 the filer never entered.

Fact.Name: The split names fewer than two or more than three accounts
Fact.Description: Arm (a) of the allocation knockout: the split is in effect but the additional collection holds no items (a one-account "split", which the form says not to file: "If you want your refund deposited to only one account, don't complete this form") or three or more (the form has lines for three accounts in all).

Fact.Name: The split is in effect but a line 1a, 2 or 3 entry is unanswered
Fact.Description: Arm (b) of the allocation knockout: the split is in effect and line 1a is unanswered, or any additional row is missing its account or its amount. Fails CLOSED: the form rejects a deposit request without a valid account and routing number, and a missing amount cannot foot.

Fact.Name: The split is in effect and a deposit is under the form's $1 floor
Fact.Description: Arm (c) of the allocation knockout: "Each deposit must be at least $1." A $0 line 1a or row amount is an account listed with nothing to deposit, which the form does not allow; the writables floor at $0 so the filer's entry is preserved and the contradiction refused rather than clamped.

Fact.Name: Form 8888 line 5 does not equal Form 1040 line 35a
Fact.Description: Arm (d) of the allocation knockout: the split is in effect, line 5 is computable, and it differs from the refund the return actually pays out, taxCalculations:/form1040Line35aRefundAfterEstimatedTaxPenalty (Form 1040 line 35a, after the line 36 carry-forward and the line 38 penalty come out of line 34; that is "the refund amount shown on your tax return", not the line 34 overpayment). Foots when equal in cents.

Fact.Name: Knockout: the Form 8888 allocation is incomplete, outside the form, or does not foot to line 35a
Fact.Description:
Refuses a return whose elected split cannot be filed as entered: (a) fewer than two or more than three accounts (/form8888AllocationRowCountOutsideForm); (b) an unanswered line 1a or a row missing its account or amount (/form8888AllocationIncomplete); (c) a deposit under $1 (/form8888AnyDepositBelowMinimum); (d) line 5 not equal to Form 1040 line 35a (/form8888AllocationDoesNotFoot). Complete-safe False on every return that does not elect the split.
PERMANENT DATA-COMPLETENESS RESIDUE. Every arm is unanswered or self-contradictory intake, and the form says what happens to such a filing: "If the total on line 5 is different, your refund may be delayed"; a missing account "will be rejected, and your refund may be delayed or deposited in the last valid account listed". This dictionary does not file a return whose refund routing it knows to be wrong. The refusal evaporates as the filer answers: with every row complete, every deposit at least $1, and line 5 equal to line 35a, it is False. Dual-wired (BlockSubmissionOnTrue here plus membership in flow:/flowIsKnockedOut).

Fact.Name: Knockout: Form 8888 is attached but this dictionary has no Form 8888 export or print template yet
Fact.Description:
Refuses every return on which the split is in effect (/form8888SplitRefundElected), until the filing carrier ships. WHY THIS EXISTS: when Form 8888 is attached the 2025 Form 1040 instructions leave lines 35b-35d blank (the either/or at "Lines 35a Through 35d"), and paymentMethod:/xmlRefundBankAccount now honours that. The accounts must therefore travel on Form 8888 itself, and this dictionary has no IRS8888 MeF export and no dictionary/pdf/2025/IRS8888 template: a split-elected return would transmit a checked line 35a box and NO account. Refuse rather than file a refund with nowhere to go (World #1). The arithmetic and the allocation knockout are complete and tested, so the successor is the carrier alone.
RETIRES when the IRS8888 export (lines 1a-1d, 2a-2d, 3a-3d, 5, reading /form8888FirstAccount, /writableFirstAccountDepositAmount, /form8888AdditionalAccounts and /form8888Line5TotalAllocation) and the print template exist; delete this fact and its flow membership in the same commit. Dual-wired (BlockSubmissionOnTrue here plus membership in flow:/flowIsKnockedOut).

Fact.Name: Trigger for the IRS8888 filing carrier: the Form 8888 split is in effect
Fact.Description:
Return-level carrier TRIGGER for the Form 8888 split. This Boolean mirrors the already-built /form8888SplitRefundElected posture so the IRS8888 MeF binding and the print carrier can consume one stable downstream fact: true only when the filer elected a split, a refund is due, and direct deposit was chosen. The Form 8888 arithmetic, account intake, and fail-closed allocation guards remain in this module.
THIS FACT DOES NOT MEAN A CARRIER EXISTS, AND SAYS SO HERE BECAUSE ITS OWN VALUE WOULD OTHERWISE IMPLY IT. It is TRUE on exactly the population /knockoutForm8888AttachedWithoutFilingCarrier refuses, and both are committed asserts on tests/nodes/ty2025/form8888/f8888-two-account-split-foots-exactly and f8888-three-account-split-foots-exactly so the contradiction is measured rather than described, and cannot resolve silently.
WHY mef="true" IS NOT ON THIS FACT OR ON THE FIVE THE CONTRACT NAMES — A SOURCE BLOCK, NOT A SCOPE ONE. Invariant 7's amendment removed the e-file/MeF clause outright, so e-file/MeF grounds no refusal and no EXTERNAL verdict in this repo (the owner's scope amendment). The actual blocker is invariant 3, no fabricated citations: no IRS8888 MeF schema is vendored. The one MeF artifact under sources/ is the IRS1040 rendering stylesheet sources/mef-irs1040-stylesheet--ty2025--2025-11.xml (4,280 lines); it names FormData/Form8888Ind, the Form 1040 line 35a checkbox, and nothing for the IRS8888 schedule, so element names for Form 8888 lines 1a-1d, 2a-2d, 3a-3d and 5 are unciteable today. That is the same bar the queued /xmlAchPaymentDate twin sits behind (paymentMethod.xml). The remedy is source acquisition; no dictionary computation is owed. Until a carrier ships, /knockoutForm8888AttachedWithoutFilingCarrier continues to refuse an elected split.
